PullRequest.Title: Agents: support multiple pull requests per session
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- choose the highest-priority status icon across all pull requests associated with a session
- combine pull request CI and review notifications into one carousel banner with scoped split actions
- hide pull request banner items while Agent Merge is enabled and show live pull request titles in session hovers

## Test plan
- covered multi-PR polling, icon priority, banner carousel/actions/dismissal/focus, Agent Merge gating, feedback scoping, and live title hydration with focused unit tests
- added combined, multi-PR, and narrow component fixtures

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, all-session ownership, uncapped source collection, 60-second model intervals, and concrete REST/GraphQL calls are directly traced. The exact number of users with large PR histories is uncertain, which limits severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST and GraphQL API calls, response bytes, and request-processing work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost grows with the number of distinct pull-request references across every unarchived session (shared model keys coalesce only duplicate references to the same PR). Each additional open PR adds two PR metadata/review REST calls, one CI call, and one review-thread GraphQL call per 60-second cycle, plus the same four-call startup burst; closed/draft PRs still add the two metadata/review calls.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive background network traffic and GitHub API rate-limit pressure, with startup bursts and delayed or failed status updates once the quota is exhausted.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each tracked session acquired and refreshed only its primary pull-request model, then polled CI and review threads only for that one PR.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added loop invokes `_pollPullRequest` for every associated PR of every unarchived session. `_pollPullRequest` immediately refreshes each model and starts independent 60-second PR/CI/review-thread polling as applicable.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The changed hunk replaced a single `{ owner, repo, prNumber }` poll setup with `for (const pullRequest of identity.pullRequests)`, so background requests changed from one PR per session to all associated PRs.
Findings.Title: Bound background polling across associated pull requests
Findings.Impact: Opening a profile with many retained agent sessions that each produced multiple PRs now starts a burst proportional to the total PR history and keeps issuing up to four GitHub requests per open PR per minute, even when those sessions are not active. A realistic set of a few dozen unique PRs can consume thousands of API requests per hour and make session icons/banners stop updating under rate limiting.
Findings.Evidence: `_onDidChangeSessions` installs a poller for every session, and `toGitHubPromotion` retains all deduplicated PR artifacts without a cardinality cap. This new loop calls `_pollPullRequest` for each ref. That helper calls `GitHubPullRequestModel.refresh()` immediately and starts its 60-second poll; the model refresh performs `getPullRequest` and `getReviews` in parallel. For every open non-draft PR it also refreshes and starts 60-second CI and review-thread models, whose fetchers cross the REST/GraphQL boundary. Reference collections prevent duplicate calls only when two sessions reference the exact same PR; they do not bound aggregate unique-PR concurrency.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep inactive sessions on the primary/cached PR presentation, and refresh all associated PRs only for the active session; alternatively route additional-PR refreshes through a shared bounded/staggered scheduler with a substantially lower inactive cadence so aggregate GitHub traffic is capped.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The unconditional added call, active-session lifetime, state gate in the existing owner, one-minute interval, and GraphQL boundary are directly visible. Only the typical number of historical PRs per session is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub GraphQL requests and review-thread/comment response payloads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For the active session, one 60-second GraphQL poll is retained for every associated PR. Shared polling suppresses duplicate timers for open PRs already owned by the GitHub polling contribution, but each additional closed, merged, or draft PR gains a new recurring request because that contribution deliberately does not poll review threads for those states.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Persistent unnecessary network traffic and GitHub API quota consumption while a multi-PR session remains active.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: CodeReviewService only consumed the primary review-thread model; polling was owned elsewhere. The existing GitHub session poller limits CI/review-thread polling to open, non-draft PRs (apart from the legacy primary active-session owner).
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new autorun refreshes and calls `startPolling()` on the review-thread model for every associated PR without checking the PR's live state.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 148 registers a polling client for each entry in `context.pullRequests`; before this PR, CodeReviewService did not start review-thread polling at all.
Findings.Title: Do not continuously poll review threads for inactive PR states
Findings.Impact: Selecting a long-running session with historical merged/closed PRs keeps a GraphQL `GetReviewThreads` request running every minute for each historical PR. The query can return up to 100 threads with up to 100 comments each, so sessions with several prior PRs continuously consume bandwidth and API quota despite those PRs no longer changing.
Findings.Evidence: The added loop calls `refresh()` and `startPolling()` unconditionally. `GitHubPullRequestReviewThreadsModel.startPolling` schedules every 60 seconds, and `_refresh` invokes `GitHubPRFetcher.getReviewThreads`, which performs a GraphQL query. By contrast, `GitHubPullRequestPollingContribution` starts review-thread polling only after `!isDraft && state === Open`; therefore model client-count coalescing does not eliminate the newly introduced polling for historical non-open PRs.
Findings.Recommendation: Refresh historical PR thread models once to populate combined state, but call `startPolling()` only for live open, non-draft PRs (or rely on the existing GitHub polling owner for those models).

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restore and background status polling for unarchived sessions with multiple associated pull requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Polling begins after workbench restore and is off the direct session-render critical path, but its unbounded startup burst and recurring traffic contend for GitHub quota and network resources used by interactive GitHub features.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch pull-request metadata and reviews through two concurrent GitHub REST requests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate pair and then one pair per minute for each distinct non-merged associated PR; merged inactive PRs still incur the initial pair.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the primary PR of each session was refreshed and polled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work is not required before list rendering, but can exhaust API quota and delay later interactive GitHub requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate request and one request per minute for every distinct open, non-draft associated PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the primary open, non-draft PR of each session was polled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial UI critical path, but status freshness depends on completion and aggregate traffic consumes API quota.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch up to 100 review threads and up to 100 comments per thread via GitHub GraphQL
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate request and one request per minute for every distinct open, non-draft associated PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the primary open, non-draft PR of each session was polled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial UI critical path, but drives status icons and can contend with interactive requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total distinct PR identities across all unarchived sessions after exact-key model sharing; agent-host metadata retains every deduplicated PR artifact for the session without a cardinality cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The per-session loop starts every PR refresh without awaiting or using a shared limiter. Each PR metadata refresh itself issues two REST requests concurrently. Shared reference models coalesce the same owner/repo/number across consumers, but distinct PRs remain fully concurrent and each model owns a 60-second scheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR and CI polling use ETags on warm refreshes, reducing response bodies on unchanged data but not request cardinality; review-thread GraphQL polling has no ETag. Reference collections coalesce identical PR keys and in-flight model refreshes, but most session-created PRs are unique.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed one-to-many loop, all-session ownership, model intervals, boundary calls, and exact-key coalescing were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The distribution of unarchived sessions and PRs produced per session is unknown; the request multiplier and absence of an aggregate limiter are explicit, so uncertainty affects severity only.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: the diff multiplies immediate and recurring GitHub calls from one PR per session to every associated PR across every unarchived session.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a multi-PR session and hydrating unresolved review comments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The PR-review state remains Loading until every associated review-thread model completes its first fetch, so the slowest request gates comment presentation. Recurring polls continue while the session is active.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch review threads and nested comments via GitHub GraphQL
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate request per associated PR and one request per minute for each model kept alive; for additional closed/merged/draft PRs this recurring traffic is newly introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: CodeReviewService consumed the primary model and did not own polling; the general session poller gates review polling to open, non-draft PRs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All initial requests must complete before combined PR review state leaves Loading; later requests update comments in the background.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of associated PRs in the active session, including historical merged, closed, and draft PRs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All model refreshes are launched together without a limiter. Shared model polling-client counts avoid a second timer for open PRs already polled elsewhere, but non-open additional PRs gain their own recurring timer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: References share one model per PR and refresh calls coalesce while in flight. The GraphQL review-thread request has no ETag or warm negative cache; every scheduled cycle fetches the thread payload again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: unconditional added startPolling call, active-session lifetime, 60-second model cadence, and GraphQL implementation are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical historical PR count and payload sizes vary, but the unconditional recurring GraphQL request for every state is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out because non-open historical PRs are continuously polled despite the existing polling owner intentionally excluding those states.

Scenarios.Scenario: Displaying and interacting with the active session's combined CI/comment banner
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Banner state reads all PR and CI models; action execution waits for the chat model and user-triggered CI annotation retrieval, while ordinary banner rendering is local.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh active-session PR and CI models
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one immediate refresh per associated PR/model when not already in flight; recurring timers are shared with the global polling owner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The banner consumed the single active-session PR/CI observables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model completion determines when CI banner details appear, but does not block chat input rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch annotations for each failed CI check before submitting a fix prompt
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per failed check for the selected PR, only after explicit user action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-failed-check annotation retrieval already existed; the diff only adds scoped/custom query support.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User-triggered action waits for all annotation requests before prompt submission.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Associated PR count, created feedback count, and failed check count for the selected PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The banner acquires shared PR/CI models and registers polling clients, but model client counts coalesce recurring timers with the global poller. Combined CI annotation reads retain their existing per-failed-check Promise.all behavior and occur only on user action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Shared references and in-flight refresh promises coalesce model work; PR/CI warm requests use ETags. Banner derivation rescans feedback per PR and rebuilds one widget, but realistic cardinality did not establish a separate CPU/rendering regression.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary ownership and coalescing; insufficient evidence for a separate render/CPU finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PR and feedback collections are usually small; no evidence showed local filtering or single-widget reconstruction alone causing visible jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the global poll fan-out: shared models prevent duplicate periodic active-banner polling, and user-triggered annotation reads are pre-existing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering session list, picker, pull-request pill, and live PR titles/icons
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Local observable derivations compute the highest-priority icon and title before affected rows/pills update; no filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, or network call is initiated directly by these render helpers.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: PR count per rendered session; computation is linear in that count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local array mapping/scanning only. Remote model updates originate from the separately analyzed pollers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live PR models are reference-shared and icon values are persisted in the icon cache; absent live data falls back to cached/provider icons and stored titles.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that changed render work is local and linear.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PR arrays are not explicitly capped, but the local O(P) scans and allocations are small compared with the network polling and lack evidence of frame-level impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submitting scoped feedback and resolving originating PR review threads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Submitting waits for chat request acceptance; resolving a feedback item issues one GitHub mutation and refresh for each transitioned/deleted thread, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve one GitHub review thread and refresh its thread model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mutation plus refresh per unique transitioned thread, deduplicated by the per-session requested set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-thread resolution occurred; the diff adds source-PR routing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs asynchronously after feedback state changes and does not block editor interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit a chat request with selected feedback attachment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per explicit banner action; selected Agent Host feedback reduces attachment cardinality, while non-Agent-Host behavior remains whole-attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One request submitted all accepted feedback; the diff scopes attachment contents without adding requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The user action waits for request acceptance.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected feedback IDs for one banner action and number of individual PR threads the user resolves.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Feedback selection uses local sets. Thread resolution is launched per qualifying feedback transition without a new aggregate scheduler, but the diff preserves the prior per-thread call cardinality and only routes each call to its source PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Feedback attachments are transient and removed on request acceptance/failure. Review models are shared by PR key and refresh after mutation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that source metadata changes routing rather than boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Thread count depends on user actions, but no changed multiplicity was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding; changed metadata and scoping do not add expensive operations.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 41 changed files and all diff pages. Reported two network fan-out regressions: all-session polling now scales with every associated PR, and active code-review hydration continuously polls non-open historical PRs. Shared model references, in-flight refresh coalescing, UI rendering, feedback submission, and resolution lifecycles were checked and did not support additional findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
